purpose: How an expert turns a site walk into a lawful, per-zone camera design and a commissioned installation the cloud subscription can stand on: coverage objectives and pixel-density targets per zone, camera and placement choices bounded by disclosed-surveillance law, edge/cloud/hybrid recording sized by bitrate, storage and measured-uplink mechanisms, a segmented and hardened camera network, and day/night commissioning with failover drills and documented handover to operations.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors

this is an own-build vertical: the designer also installs and then operates the cloud recording subscription, so every design choice is judged by whether the site stays supportable for years, not just by whether the install closes
all surveillance designed here is lawful and disclosed, serving deterrence, detection and evidence for the property owner; covert or unlawful monitoring requests are refused at intake
camera-placement, video-privacy and audio-consent law vary sharply by jurisdiction, so every design carries a verify-current-rules-locally flag instead of embedded legal specifics
bitrates, storage volumes and bandwidth figures are treated as mechanisms computed from each site's own measurements, never as invented universal numbers stated as fact
the premises, network and internet uplink are as found at survey; a material premises change re-opens the affected design decisions
exclusions: subscription tier construction, segment targeting, the build-on-VSaaS-platform versus own-stack business decision, pricing architecture and selling practice - that is KB1 (Surveillance Offer Design & Subscription Pricing) territory; this KB hands it a design package with counts and assumptions, never prices

running the recurring service - camera-health monitoring, storage and retention management in operation, incident retrieval workflow, footage-access audit, renewals and churn - that is KB3 (Cloud Video Operations & Privacy Compliance) territory; this KB fixes retention and access decisions at design time and hands them off
covert, hidden or otherwise unlawful surveillance design of any kind, including workarounds that aim sensors at privacy-expectation zones or monitor people beyond the owner's property interest
jurisdiction-specific legal advice on video privacy, audio consent, employee notification or signage wording - obligation classes are named and flagged verify-locally, never asserted as local rules
stated per-camera, per-license or per-gigabyte price points - equipment and platform costs appear only as mechanisms and qualitative bands
monitoring of identified individuals rather than protection of property, including covert domestic-surveillance requests
alarm and intrusion panels, access-control hardware and other non-video security trades, except where they share mounting, power or network infrastructure with the camera estate

competency_questions.question: What must the site survey and uplink measurement capture before any camera design is drawn?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SITE_SURVEY_INTAKE lists the physical, electrical, lighting and constraint facts the walk must record, and UPLINK_QUALIFICATION explains why the upstream path is measured at the worst relevant hour rather than assumed

competency_questions.question: How is an owner's vague wish to protect the property turned into a per-zone coverage design with accepted gaps?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COVERAGE_OBJECTIVES_MAP assigns each zone a deter/detect/identify purpose and records accepted blind spots, and SITE_DESIGN_SPEC shows where those decisions are consolidated

competency_questions.question: Where may cameras not look or listen, and how does the design handle jurisdiction-to-jurisdiction variation in surveillance law?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LAWFUL_PLACEMENT_BOUNDARY names privacy-expectation zones, neighbor-overlook care, the audio-consent obligation classes and the verify-locally flag, and states that covert requests are declined

competency_questions.question: How are pixel-density targets set per zone and how do they drive camera and lens selection?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PIXEL_DENSITY_TARGETS explains on-target density as the mechanism behind deter/detect/identify capability with the published DORI bands as reference, and CAMERA_SELECTION shows sensor, lens, form factor and WDR choices executing those targets

competency_questions.question: How are cameras placed and aimed - height, tilt, choke points, light - so entrances actually yield identification-grade footage?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PLACEMENT_GEOMETRY gives the height/angle/choke-point rules including the hat-top failure of eave mounting, and LIGHTING_AND_SCENE covers night-scene engineering, IR pitfalls and backlight

competency_questions.question: When does a site record at the edge, in the cloud, or hybrid, and what facts drive that choice?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RECORDING_ARCHITECTURE weighs offsite-evidence value, measured uplink, outage tolerance and theft/fire exposure of local storage, and names hybrid with an edge buffer as the usual answer for thin uplinks

competency_questions.question: How is it computed whether a design's stream load and retention fit the site's uplink and storage, and what gets cut when the math fails?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BANDWIDTH_STORAGE_MATH states the bitrate, duty-cycle, retention and headroom mechanisms with the site's own measurements as inputs, and UPLINK_QUALIFICATION supplies the measured budget the load must fit under

competency_questions.question: How are retention length and who-may-view decided at design time, and how do those decisions reach the operations side?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RETENTION_ACCESS_DESIGN treats retention days per zone class and the authorized-viewer list as first-class design outputs under named data-protection obligation classes, handed off via the design spec and as-built package

competency_questions.question: How is the camera estate kept from becoming the weakest point of the customer's network?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NETWORK_SEGMENTATION isolates cameras on their own segment with outbound-only cloud flows and no route to the business LAN, and CAMERA_HARDENING states the per-device baseline: unique credentials, current firmware, disabled services, verified encrypted transport and NTP

competency_questions.question: What does installation-grade power budgeting, cabling and mounting look like, and why does it protect subscription margin?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: POWER_POE_BUDGET budgets at worst-case draw with UPS backing, CABLING_STANDARDS states the workmanship standard from sealed glands to labeled certified runs, and MOUNTING_INSTALL_QUALITY ties workmanship to avoided truck rolls

competency_questions.question: What tests must every camera and the whole site pass before handover?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMMISSIONING_TESTS requires day and night per-camera checks, end-to-end cloud clip retrieval, timestamp verification, the uplink-pull failover drill, and hardening spot-checks, with failures looping back to design nodes

competency_questions.question: When can existing cameras and cabling be kept on a takeover site, and when must they be retired?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EXISTING_SYSTEM_TAKEOVER gives per-component reuse tests against platform integration, the hardening baseline and restricted-vendor procurement classes, with keep/retire verdicts in writing

competency_questions.question: What does the customer sign off on at handover, and which documents move to the recurring service?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: VIEW_ACCEPTANCE_WALKTHROUGH demonstrates each coverage objective on screen with capability honesty and restated retention/access decisions, and AS_BUILT_DOCUMENTATION lists the record set operations needs to service the site without the installer's memory

glossary.definition: The published detection / observation / recognition / identification pixel-density reference scale from the IEC 62676 standard family, used to size how many pixels must land on a subject for each zone purpose; a sizing mechanism, not a promise of analytics.

The pixels per unit of subject width that a camera delivers at the subject's actual distance; the quantity that decides whether a view can identify a face rather than merely detect that someone moved.
Sensor and processing capability that holds detail when one scene mixes bright and dark, such as a glass storefront door with daylight glare behind incoming faces.
An adjustable-focal-length lens set during installation to match a zone's field of view and density target, in contrast to a fixed lens whose framing is locked at purchase.

The total and per-port power a Power-over-Ethernet switch can actually deliver, compared against the summed worst-case draw of its cameras with IR illuminators and heaters running, not their idle draw.
The isolated network segment that carries only camera and recorder traffic, firewalled so cameras reach the cloud outbound-only and can never touch the business LAN or POS segment.

Local recording on a camera's storage card or a small on-site store that continues through an uplink outage and then uploads the missed span to the cloud once the line returns, closing the evidence gap.
The data rate of a camera's encoded stream, driven by resolution, frame rate, codec class and scene complexity; the single number that couples image ambition to uplink and storage reality.

The written day-and-night test pass - per-camera views, end-to-end cloud clip retrieval, timestamps, the uplink-pull failover drill and hardening spot-checks - that must succeed before handover and invoicing.

The record set delivered at handoff - camera schedule, port map, network diagram, sizing sheet, configured policies and commissioning report - that lets the site be serviced for years without the installer's memory.

nodes.definition: Walk the property with the owner before any design is drawn and capture the facts the whole design hangs on: what is being protected and why (shrink at the till, tools in the yard, a break-in history), building layout with every entrance, exit, receiving door and sight line, mounting surfaces and ceiling types, existing conduit and cable paths, power availability near likely mounting points, where the router and any rack live, ambient lighting by day and by night, and environmental exposure such as eaves, dust, coastal salt or wash-down zones. The walk also surfaces constraints owners rarely volunteer: landlord permission for penetrations, facade aesthetics on a customer-facing frontage, and areas staff regard as private. The output is a survey record with photos and a floor sketch that every later design node cites instead of re-visiting the site.

included: physical, electrical and network constraint capture
excluded: drawing the camera design itself
quoting or pricing the job

pros.claim: A measured survey turns design from guesswork into placement against known surfaces, power and sight lines
pros.example: discovering on the walk that the yard floodlight dies at 22:00 reshapes the whole night-coverage approach before a single camera is ordered

cons.claim: A thorough survey spends unpaid pre-sale hours on prospects who never sign
cons.example: a two-hour walk plus write-up for a cafe owner who then buys a consumer DIY kit online

failure_modes: surveying only in daylight and never seeing the night scene the cameras must survive
trusting the owner's memory of the layout instead of walking every zone
taking no photos, so the designer re-visits the site for every later question
acceptance_tests: the survey record contains a floor sketch, per-zone photos, power/mounting/network notes, incident history and the owner's stated protection goals
revisit_triggers: the premises are remodeled or a new tenancy changes landlord rules
an incident occurs that changes what the owner wants protected

base.update_signal: a premises change, new landlord or tenancy rules, or a fresh incident invalidates the survey record

nodes.definition: Convert the owner's protection goals into a per-zone coverage objective map before any hardware is discussed: each zone - entrances and exits, POS and cash handling, receiving door, stockroom, yard and laydown areas, parking, perimeter approaches - gets a stated purpose of deter, detect or identify, because purpose decides everything downstream: a yard needs wide detection, an entrance needs identification-grade capture at its choke point, and the POS needs hands-and-till detail. The map also names explicitly what is NOT covered - blind spots accepted on cost or lawfulness grounds - so the owner accepts residual gaps knowingly at design time instead of discovering them after an incident. This map is the contract the pixel math, placement plan and acceptance walkthrough are all checked against.

excluded: camera model choice
lawfulness screening, which the lawful-placement node owns

pros.claim: Purpose-per-zone prevents the classic failure of many cameras but no usable footage
pros.example: one identification camera at the single entrance choke point outperforms four wide overview cameras the day the police ask who it was

cons.claim: Zone-by-zone rigor costs design time a small job's margin barely carries
cons.example: a full mapping exercise for a two-camera residential side-gate job is mostly overhead

failure_modes: designing coverage around where mounting is easy rather than where objectives point
leaving accepted blind spots undocumented so they surface as complaints after a theft
marking every zone identify and tripling the camera count without need
acceptance_tests: every zone in the map carries a deter/detect/identify purpose and the accepted-gap list is signed into the design record
revisit_triggers: an incident occurs in a zone whose gap was accepted
the owner adds zones such as a new yard, till or storage container

base.update_signal: the owner's protection priorities change or an accepted gap produces an incident

nodes.definition: Screen every proposed view against the lawful-and-disclosed boundary before geometry is fixed: no coverage of privacy-expectation zones (restrooms, changing rooms and, in many jurisdictions, staff break areas), no covert or hidden devices of any kind, deliberate care with views that overlook a neighbor's windows or garden or sweep public sidewalk beyond the owner's property interest, and an explicit audio decision, because audio capture sits under consent regimes (one-party and all-party consent classes) that differ sharply by jurisdiction and is usually left disabled. The screen names the obligation classes in play - placement limits, employee-notification duties, signage and disclosure duties, audio consent - and stamps every design with a verify-current-rules-in-this-jurisdiction flag; this KB never asserts local law. A covert-monitoring request is declined at intake and logged, not negotiated.

excluded: jurisdiction-specific legal advice or signage wording
the operational access-audit regime, which the operations KB runs

pros.claim: The screen rules out designs a court, a regulator or an employee complaint would later unwind
pros.example: catching at design review that a warehouse camera's wide view takes in the neighbor's fenced yard, and re-aiming before a bracket is drilled

cons.claim: The boundary removes genuinely wanted coverage and can cost the sale
cons.example: an owner who insists on a hidden break-room camera to catch a suspected employee hears no and may walk to a less scrupulous installer

failure_modes: masking a forbidden zone in software while the sensor still captures it, where the rules treat capture itself as the violation
shipping audio enabled by default because the camera happens to have a microphone
reusing a template design across jurisdictions without re-running the local check
acceptance_tests: the design shows zero privacy-expectation-zone coverage, a recorded audio decision, the verify-locally flag, and any covert request logged as declined
revisit_triggers: a jurisdiction changes its placement, consent or signage rules
a staff or neighbor complaint about an existing view arrives
a new zone type such as a shared-tenancy corridor enters a design

base.update_signal: a surveillance, privacy or consent rule changes in a served jurisdiction, or a complaint tests an existing design

nodes.definition: Measure - never assume - the upstream path the cloud subscription will live on: run upstream throughput tests at business-peak hours as well as quiet hours, note the ISP plan's asymmetry (upload is the scarce side), data caps and their overage behavior, CGNAT presence (which kills inbound access and pushes the design to outbound-only cloud connections regardless), router quality and who controls it, and competing site load such as cloud backups or music streaming during trading hours. The measured worst-relevant-hour upstream figure, minus a stated headroom share reserved for the business's own operations, becomes the budget every stream in the bandwidth math must fit under; a site whose uplink cannot carry any useful cloud stream is flagged early for an edge-heavy architecture or an uplink upgrade conversation before promises are made.

excluded: negotiating the customer's ISP contract
the recording-architecture decision itself

pros.claim: Measuring at the worst relevant hour exposes the uplink the cameras will actually get
pros.example: a 19:00 test shows the sports bar's uplink saturating exactly when cameras matter most, steering the design to hybrid before the sale closes

cons.claim: Peak-hour measurement takes coordination and still samples a limited window
cons.example: a single Tuesday-evening test misses the Saturday crowd that doubles the site's competing traffic

failure_modes: designing on the ISP's advertised speed instead of a measurement
measuring downstream and calling it the uplink
missing a second tenant who shares the same line and its capacity
acceptance_tests: a dated upstream measurement at the worst relevant hour exists, with cap/CGNAT/router notes and a stated headroom share, and the resulting uplink budget is written into the design spec
revisit_triggers: the ISP plan, router or line changes
a new tenant or new site load appears on the connection
operations reports upload backlog alarms after handover

base.update_signal: a re-measurement, an ISP plan change, or a post-handover upload backlog contradicts the recorded uplink budget

nodes.definition: Translate each zone's purpose into an on-target pixel-density requirement - the mechanism that decides whether footage can actually deter, detect or identify: density falls with distance and thins as field of view widens, and identification demands several times the on-target density that plain detection needs, so the published DORI bands of the IEC 62676 family serve as the reference scale instead of folklore. From the target density plus the zone's real measured distances and scene width, derive required resolution and focal length, choose fixed versus varifocal, and mark the zones where one camera mathematically cannot deliver both wide context and identify-grade detail so they get a pair - a context view plus a choke-point detail view - rather than a promise the sensor cannot keep.

included: per-zone density target against the DORI reference
resolution and focal-length derivation from measured distances
excluded: final camera model choice
bitrate and storage consequences, which the sizing math owns

pros.claim: Density math turns a vague HD-should-be-fine instinct into a checkable design
pros.example: the math shows a 2-megapixel wide view cannot identify at the driveway gate's distance, so a dedicated tighter camera is specified before install day

cons.claim: A target met on paper can still fail in the physical scene
cons.example: a formally sufficient entrance view smeared to uselessness by night gain noise and a dirty dome

failure_modes: quoting DORI numbers without measuring the zone's actual distances
assuming digital zoom adds pixels that the sensor never captured
sizing for the nearest point of a zone while incidents happen at its far edge
acceptance_tests: each zone's target density, measured distance and derived resolution/focal choice are recorded, and zones needing a context-plus-detail pair are flagged
revisit_triggers: a zone's purpose is upgraded, e.g. from detect to identify after an incident
commissioning footage shows the computed density was not achieved in practice

base.update_signal: commissioning or incident footage shows a zone's achieved density missing its target, or a zone purpose changes

nodes.definition: Pick each zone's camera as the intersection of its density target, scene and mounting reality rather than by catalog habit: form factor by exposure and tamper picture (turret over dome outdoors where IR bounce inside a bubble washes night images, vandal-rated dome at hand height, bullet for long narrow throws, PTZ only where someone actively operates it since a PTZ parked wrong is a blind spot), sensor and lens by the zone's density target and light (a larger sensor and honest low-light ability beat headline megapixels in a dim yard; WDR class at glass-door entrances), infrared versus white-light illumination by whether deterrence or discretion serves the owner - disclosed either way - environmental ingress and impact protection classes by mounting exposure, and microphone capability handled strictly under the lawful screen's audio-consent decision. Every choice is written against the zone objective it serves so procurement substitutions can be checked instead of silently degrading the design; models are compared by mechanism - sensor size, aperture, illuminator range class, codec support - never by invented price points.

included: form factor, sensor, lens and illumination choice per zone
excluded: price negotiation and margin, which the offer KB owns
network and hardening configuration

pros.claim: Choosing by zone mechanism instead of catalog habit prevents quiet capability loss
pros.example: a turret with a larger sensor rescues the dim loading dock where the habitual dome model produced IR-fogged night footage

cons.claim: Model diversity across zones raises stocking and spares complexity for a small installer
cons.example: five camera models on one site means five spare types on the van and five firmware tracks to follow

failure_modes: specifying a PTZ for an unmanned site where it parks facing the wrong way during the incident
buying megapixels instead of sensor size for a night-critical yard
letting a procurement substitution swap a WDR entrance camera for a non-WDR lookalike
acceptance_tests: each specified model is written against the zone objective it serves with the sensor/lens/illumination reasoning stated, so substitutions are checkable
revisit_triggers: a specified model is discontinued or its firmware track goes stale
a zone purpose or lighting verdict changes upstream

base.update_signal: a model discontinuation, firmware advisory, or upstream zone change forces a re-selection

nodes.definition: Fix each camera's exact mounting point, height and tilt so geometry serves the objective: identification shots come from near face height at choke points where a doorway forces distance and angle, not from eave height where caps and foreheads defeat the purpose; overview cameras sit high for reach but never frame the horizon or sky, which wastes half the sensor; entrances get an in-and-out pairing - a face camera on incomers and a second view catching exits; aim axes avoid rising and setting sun and mirror glass; the lawful screen's excluded zones are honored by physical aiming, not only by software mask; and every camera goes where a ladder can service it but a casual reach cannot. The placement plan records height, tilt and the expected on-target density per view so the install crew executes geometry, not vibes.

included: mount point, height and tilt per camera
excluded: anchor and sealing workmanship, which the mounting node owns
scene lighting changes, which the lighting node owns

pros.claim: Choke-point geometry at face height is what turns an entrance camera into evidence
pros.example: moving the doorway camera from the soffit to just above head height converts a month of cap-top footage into usable faces

cons.claim: Low identification mounting raises tamper exposure that must then be managed
cons.example: the face-height camera beside a bar entrance gets knocked askew monthly and needs a vandal housing and re-aim checks

failure_modes: framing the horizon so half the pixels record sky
mounting under an overhang whose surface flares the built-in IR
relying on a software privacy mask while the physical aim still sweeps a forbidden zone
acceptance_tests: the placement plan states height, tilt and expected on-target density for every camera, and entrance zones show an in-and-out pairing or a recorded reason why not
revisit_triggers: commissioning shows a view missing its expected framing or density
a lawful-screen change or premises change moves an allowed aim envelope

base.update_signal: commissioning framing failures, tamper incidents, or a changed aim envelope re-open the placement plan

nodes.definition: Engineer the scene, not just the camera: assess each view by day and after dark for the failure sources that ruin footage - IR bounce off near walls and eaves, insects and spider webs drawn to built-in IR, headlight bloom at driveways, mirror-glass reflections, flickering discharge or cheap LED lighting, and full darkness beyond IR reach in large yards. Decide per zone whether to fix the scene or upgrade the sensor: adding or re-tasking a modest luminaire, moving the aim, or mounting external IR off-axis is often cheaper than exotic low-light glass and doubles as deterrence, while a genuinely dark wide yard may justify a true low-light sensor instead. Light spill and glare toward neighbors is noted as a courtesy and, in some places, an obligation class of its own - verify locally.

included: day and night scene assessment per view
excluded: electrical installation of new lighting circuits beyond camera-scope fixtures
camera model selection itself

pros.claim: A small lighting fix often outperforms an expensive camera upgrade at night
pros.example: re-tasking an existing yard floodlight onto the container area turns a noisy IR scene into clean color footage

cons.claim: Scene changes touch things the installer does not fully control
cons.example: the landlord's sodium floodlight on a timer overrides the design's assumption every winter evening

failure_modes: assessing scenes only in daylight
mounting cameras with built-in IR under reflective eaves and calling the washout a camera fault
aiming a floodlight so it blinds the camera it was meant to help
acceptance_tests: every view carries a night-scene verdict: acceptable as-is, scene fix specified, or low-light sensor specified
revisit_triggers: site lighting changes, e.g. a fixture fails or the landlord swaps luminaires
seasonal change moves darkness into operating hours

base.update_signal: a night commissioning failure or a site lighting change contradicts a recorded scene verdict

nodes.definition: When a site already has cameras, produce an honest per-component reuse verdict instead of a blanket rip-out or blanket keep: existing IP cameras are tested against the cloud platform's integration path (ONVIF profile support, codec, RTSP behavior) and against the hardening baseline (changeable credentials, maintained firmware, no hard-coded callbacks to unknown parties); legacy analog coax plant can sometimes serve modest-purpose zones through encoders, but rewiring wins wherever identification zones are at stake; inherited cabling is tested and certified before being trusted. Units that cannot meet the hardening baseline, or whose provenance falls under restricted-vendor procurement classes that apply to some customer types - verify locally - are retired. The verdict sheet tells the owner what is kept, what is retired and why, and feeds the offer's economics without this KB pricing anything.

excluded: pricing the reuse savings, which the offer KB owns
ongoing support of kept legacy gear, which operations runs

pros.claim: Honest reuse where it passes the tests cuts install cost and disruption
pros.example: keeping sound conduit runs and back boxes while renewing the cameras themselves saves a day of ladder work in a finished ceiling

cons.claim: A mixed old-and-new estate multiplies support burden for the subscription
cons.example: one legacy encoder brand that drops offline weekly ends up dominating the site's service tickets

failure_modes: promising reuse before testing integration and hardening on the actual units
keeping a camera whose only admin credential is hard-coded
trusting inherited cable that was never terminated to standard
acceptance_tests: every legacy component carries a tested keep or retire verdict with its reason, and the sheet is part of the design spec
revisit_triggers: a kept component starts failing in service
a procurement or vendor-restriction class newly applies to the customer

base.update_signal: a kept legacy component fails in service or a vendor-restriction class newly applies to the site

nodes.definition: Decide at design time - as a first-class deliverable, never an afterthought - how long footage is kept and who may view it, because both drive sizing and the shape of the recurring service: a retention target per zone class (an evidence-driven entrance may warrant longer holding than an ambient yard view), whether motion-event-only retention is acceptable per zone or continuous recording is required, who the owner authorizes for live viewing versus recorded playback, expected export and evidence-handling needs, and where the jurisdiction's data-protection obligation classes - retention proportionality, subject-access rights, signage duties - bear on the choice, flagged verify-locally rather than asserted. The decisions are written into the design spec and handed to operations; the sibling operations KB runs them day to day, this KB fixes them and sizes for them.

excluded: operating the retention and access-audit regime, which the operations KB owns
cloud plan price points

pros.claim: Fixing retention and access before sizing prevents the plan from being resold twice
pros.example: agreeing thirty-day entrance retention up front sizes the cloud plan once, instead of renegotiating storage after the owner discovers week-old footage already expired

cons.claim: Owners rarely arrive with retention opinions, so the conversation takes guided effort
cons.example: a restaurant owner shrugs at retention until walked through how long a card-fraud dispute typically takes to surface

failure_modes: leaving retention to a platform default that fits neither evidence needs nor proportionality duties
granting every manager live and playback access because it was easy at setup
sizing storage before retention is agreed and then re-quoting
acceptance_tests: the design spec states retention days per zone class, continuous/event verdicts, the authorized-viewer list, and the verify-locally flags on the named obligation classes
revisit_triggers: a data-protection obligation class changes in the jurisdiction
the owner's evidence needs change, e.g. after a dispute exceeds the retention window

base.update_signal: an obligation-class change or an evidence need outgrowing the retention window re-opens the policy

nodes.definition: Choose where video lives per site as a mechanism-driven decision among edge, cloud and hybrid: pure cloud maximizes offsite evidence - a stolen recorder takes the evidence with it, the cloud copy survives - and matches the subscription this business sells, but it stands entirely on the measured uplink; pure edge (on-camera cards or a local recorder) survives uplink loss and carries high bitrates cheaply, but is stealable, fire-exposed and hollows out the recurring service's value; hybrid - cameras or a small local store buffering continuously while the cloud holds the protected copy as continuous, event-driven, or substream-continuous-plus-mainstream-event upload - is the usual honest answer for thin uplinks. Decision inputs are the measured uplink budget, retention targets, camera count and bitrate class, outage tolerance, theft and fire exposure of local storage, and the platform's supported modes; the chosen architecture is recorded with its reasoning so a later dispute reads a decision, not a memory.

included: edge/cloud/hybrid choice per site with reasoning
excluded: the arithmetic itself, which the sizing node runs
platform contract terms and pricing

pros.claim: Hybrid with an edge buffer keeps evidence offsite without oversubscribing a thin uplink
pros.example: substream-continuous upload with mainstream event clips gives a rural yard cloud evidence on an uplink that could never carry six full mainstreams

cons.claim: Hybrid doubles the components that must be commissioned and monitored
cons.example: an edge card that silently failed months ago is only discovered during the outage it existed to cover

failure_modes: selling cloud-continuous on an uplink that was never measured
leaving the only recording on a local recorder that the burglar carries out the door
choosing a mode the platform technically lists but poorly supports
acceptance_tests: the architecture decision is recorded per site with its inputs (uplink budget, retention, outage tolerance, theft/fire exposure) and the chosen upload mode
revisit_triggers: the uplink budget changes materially
the platform adds or deprecates an upload mode
an outage or theft event tests the chosen architecture

base.update_signal: an uplink change, a platform mode change, or a real outage/theft event challenges the recorded architecture decision

nodes.definition: Size the design with the actual mechanism instead of a vendor calculator taken on faith: per-camera bitrate emerges from resolution times frame rate times codec efficiency (H.265-class codecs roughly halve H.264-class bitrates at like quality) times scene complexity, where night gain noise and busy scenes inflate bitrate or degrade quality at a cap; storage need is the sum over cameras of bitrate times recorded-hours share (continuous versus motion-event duty cycle) times retention days; and cloud upload load is the sum of streams actually sent upstream, which must fit inside the measured uplink budget minus the stated headroom - with catch-up upload bursts after outages counted, since a buffer that can never drain is a fiction. The math runs on the site's own measured numbers and lives as a sizing sheet in the design spec: mechanisms and site-specific bands, never invented universal figures presented as fact.

included: upstream load versus uplink-budget check with catch-up bursts
excluded: choosing the architecture, which is upstream
cloud plan pricing

pros.claim: Running the mechanism on site numbers catches designs that vendor defaults wave through
pros.example: the sheet shows eight continuous mainstreams need triple the measured uplink budget, so six zones move to event upload before anything ships

cons.claim: Scene-complexity factors are estimates until the site runs
cons.example: a tree over the driveway doubles night event volume against the sheet's assumption every windy week

failure_modes: sizing with daytime bitrates and drowning at night
forgetting catch-up bursts so every outage creates a permanent backlog
quoting storage from a codec setting the cameras do not actually ship
acceptance_tests: a sizing sheet exists with per-camera bitrate, duty cycle, retention, summed storage, summed upstream load, the uplink budget and remaining headroom, all from site-specific inputs
revisit_triggers: measured post-install bitrates or event volumes deviate from the sheet
retention targets or camera count change

base.update_signal: post-install measured bitrates, event volumes, or backlog behavior contradict the sizing sheet

nodes.definition: Keep the camera estate off the customer's business network: a dedicated VLAN or a physically separate switch fabric carries cameras and any recorder, with the firewall passing only what the chosen architecture needs - outbound-only connections from cameras or gateway to the cloud service, no inbound port forwarding, no UPnP, no vendor peer-to-peer channels the design did not choose. The business LAN cannot reach camera admin interfaces except through a defined management path, and cameras can never reach the POS or office segment at all, so a camera compromise cannot become a card-data or file-server incident. On sites with no managed network gear, the design brings its own small managed switch and router rather than inheriting a flat home-grade LAN it cannot secure.

included: camera VLAN or separate fabric design
bring-your-own managed gear on flat sites
excluded: the customer's wider IT network design
per-device credential and firmware work, which hardening owns

pros.claim: Isolation converts a camera compromise from a business breach into a contained nuisance
pros.example: a vulnerable camera on its own VLAN cannot touch the shop's card terminal even if fully taken over

cons.claim: Segmentation on customer-owned gear adds coordination and sometimes hardware cost
cons.example: the cafe's ISP-supplied router cannot do VLANs, so the design must add a small managed switch and its configuration burden

failure_modes: dropping cameras onto the flat business LAN to save an afternoon
opening inbound port forwards for remote viewing instead of outbound cloud relay
leaving vendor P2P enabled so the estate phones home around the firewall
acceptance_tests: the network design shows cameras on an isolated segment, outbound-only flows to the cloud, no inbound forwards or UPnP, and a defined management path; a scan from the business LAN reaches no camera admin interface
revisit_triggers: the customer changes routers or ISP equipment
the platform's connectivity requirements change

base.update_signal: a router/ISP change on site or a platform connectivity change breaks the recorded segmentation design

nodes.definition: Apply a written per-device hardening baseline at install: factory credentials changed to unique per-device secrets held in the company vault - never a shared fleet password, because one leaked password must not open every customer's cameras; firmware brought current at commissioning with the version recorded; unused services disabled (telnet, UPnP, vendor P2P where the architecture does not use it); encrypted transport to the cloud verified rather than assumed; NTP time sync configured so evidence timestamps hold up when it matters; onboard microphones disabled unless the lawful screen recorded a consent-covered audio decision; and physical reset buttons weighed in tamper placement. Provenance is part of the baseline: models under restricted-vendor procurement classes for some customer types are avoided where those classes apply - verify locally.

included: credential, firmware, service, transport and NTP baseline per device
microphone-off default under the audio decision
excluded: network segment design, which is upstream
ongoing patch management after handover, which operations runs from the as-built record

pros.claim: Unique vaulted credentials cap the blast radius of any single leak
pros.example: a technician's departed-employee laptop exposes one site's vault entries for rotation, not a fleet password that opens every customer

cons.claim: Per-device rigor slows installs and depends on discipline under time pressure
cons.example: the last two cameras of a long day are the ones found still wearing factory credentials at the commissioning spot-check

failure_modes: one shared password across the whole installed base
shipping the firmware the box arrived with, vulnerabilities included
leaving a debug service enabled because disabling it was one menu deeper
acceptance_tests: every device passes the baseline checklist: unique vaulted credentials, recorded current firmware, disabled unused services, verified encrypted transport, NTP set, microphone state matching the audio decision
revisit_triggers: a vulnerability advisory lands for a deployed model class
a vendor-restriction or procurement class newly applies to a served customer type

base.update_signal: a firmware advisory, a credential-handling incident, or a new procurement restriction forces a baseline update

nodes.definition: Budget power at worst case, not nameplate idle: each camera's maximum draw with IR illuminators on, heater or blower running and any lens motor moving is summed against the PoE switch's total budget and per-port class limits with real headroom, because a switch that browns out at winter nightfall reboots cameras exactly when they are needed; long runs and thin cable add voltage drop, and PoE never runs past the roughly 100-meter twisted-pair channel limit without a powered midspan or a fiber conversion. The switch, router or gateway and any local recorder sit on a right-sized UPS so short outages neither blind the site nor corrupt local storage - and the UPS runtime must actually support the edge-buffer story the architecture promised. Surge protection on outdoor runs shields the estate from induced spikes.

included: UPS sizing for switch, gateway and recorder
excluded: mains electrical work beyond low-voltage scope
cable routing workmanship, which the cabling node owns

pros.claim: Max-draw budgeting removes a whole class of ghost faults before they exist
pros.example: a switch sized for IR-plus-heater winter draw never produces the random midnight reboots that haunt idle-budgeted installs

cons.claim: Worst-case sizing costs more up front than the cheap unmanaged alternative
cons.example: the higher-budget PoE switch and UPS look like padding on the quote until the first winter proves them

failure_modes: summing idle draws and hitting the budget wall on the first cold night
running a PoE camera past the channel limit and blaming the camera for flapping
backing up the recorder but not the switch, so cameras die anyway during an outage
acceptance_tests: the power sheet shows per-camera max draw, per-port and total switch budget with headroom, run lengths within the channel limit, and a UPS runtime figure matching the designed buffer window
revisit_triggers: cameras are added or swapped for higher-draw models
an outage reveals UPS runtime below the designed window

base.update_signal: a camera addition, a higher-draw swap, or an outage exposing short UPS runtime re-opens the power sheet

nodes.definition: Hold the cable plant to a written standard because the cable outlives every camera on it: outdoor-rated or conduited runs with UV protection, drip loops and sealed glands at every exterior entry, penetrations sealed against weather and pests, separation from mains runs to avoid induced noise, service loops at both ends, strain relief at terminations, every run labeled identically at both ends against the port map, terminations tested and certified with results kept, and paths chosen to resist casual cutting - concealed or conduited wherever a hand or a knife can reach. On takeover sites, inherited cabling passes the same certification or is renewed; an uncertified run is a fault waiting to be billed as a camera problem.

included: cable spec, routing, sealing, separation, labeling, certification
excluded: mains electrical wiring
camera aiming and mounting hardware, which the mounting node owns

pros.claim: Certified, labeled runs make every future fault a ten-minute lookup instead of a wall-opening hunt
pros.example: a flapping port traces through matching labels to a water-filled gland in minutes, on the first truck roll instead of the third

cons.claim: Standard-grade cabling takes visibly longer than staple-and-go
cons.example: conduit, glands and certification add hours the customer watching the clock did not expect on install day

failure_modes: unsealed exterior penetrations that let water track down the cable into the gland
unlabeled runs that turn every later fault into archaeology
cable stapled along a reachable fence line where one knife cut blinds the yard
acceptance_tests: every run is labeled at both ends against the port map and has a kept certification result; exterior entries show drip loops and sealed glands in the install photos
revisit_triggers: a cabling-related fault pattern appears in service tickets
premises changes cut or expose existing runs

base.update_signal: service tickets tracing to cable faults or a premises change exposing runs re-open the cabling standard's application

nodes.definition: Mount hardware as if the company will service it for a decade on subscription - because it will: anchors matched to the substrate (masonry, cladding, soffit, pole) with weight and wind load in mind, boxes and mounts sealed so water cannot track into glands, cameras leveled so the horizon does not tilt in evidence clips, cable entries hidden or conduited to deter cutting, tamper-conscious height per the placement plan, landlord and facade rules from the survey honored, and the finished install photographed per camera for the as-built record. Sloppy mounting is the classic source of margin-eating truck rolls: fogged domes from unsealed boxes, aims that sag after the first storm, and brackets that work loose on a vibrating pole.

excluded: placement decisions themselves, which are upstream
structural building work beyond camera mounts

pros.claim: Sealed, anchored, leveled mounts hold their aim and their weatherproofing for years
pros.example: the pole camera with a proper wrap-around bracket and sealed box is still on target after two storm seasons while the strap-mounted one next door points at the ground

cons.claim: Workmanship time competes with the schedule on multi-site rollouts
cons.example: sealing and photographing every mount adds most of an hour per site across a five-site chain install

failure_modes: wrong anchors for the substrate so the bracket loosens within a season
unsealed drill penetrations that fog the dome from inside
mounting where only a scaffold can ever service the unit again
acceptance_tests: each camera has a level, sealed, substrate-matched mount verified in the per-camera install photo set
revisit_triggers: a mount-related fault appears in service
facade or landlord rules change what may be fixed where

base.update_signal: mount-related service faults or changed facade rules re-open the mounting approach

nodes.definition: Prove the system before handover with a written per-camera and whole-site test pass. Per camera: focus and framing checked on a real monitor against the zone objective in daylight AND after dark, because night IR and low-light behavior differ from day; motion and event zones tuned and walk-tested at their edges; a clip recorded and retrieved end-to-end from the cloud service; timestamp accuracy against NTP verified. Whole site: the uplink-pull drill - disconnect the WAN, confirm edge buffering, reconnect, confirm catch-up upload with no gap beyond the designed window; a power-blip check on the UPS; health monitoring and alerting registered so the operations service actually sees the site from day one; and hardening spot-checks - a factory-credential login attempt fails, camera admin is unreachable from the business LAN. Failures loop back to placement, lighting or architecture; they are never waved through to make an invoice date.

excluded: the customer-facing walkthrough, which follows a passed commissioning
ongoing health monitoring, which operations runs

pros.claim: The uplink-pull drill proves the failover story instead of assuming it
pros.example: pulling the WAN at commissioning exposes an edge card formatted wrong that would otherwise have been discovered during a real outage with footage lost

cons.claim: A full day-and-night pass forces a second visit or a late evening on every install
cons.example: the crew finishes at 15:00 but the night IR check cannot happen before 21:00 in summer

failure_modes: commissioning only in daylight and shipping a night-blind site
checking the live view but never retrieving a stored clip from the cloud end
skipping the failover drill because the uplink felt fine
acceptance_tests: a commissioning report shows every camera passing day and night framing, event tuning, cloud clip retrieval and timestamp checks, plus the site-level uplink-pull, power-blip, monitoring-registration and hardening spot-checks
revisit_triggers: any camera or drill fails and returns from the fix
operations reports early-life faults that a commissioning check should have caught

base.update_signal: an early-life fault pattern that commissioning should have caught forces a checklist revision

nodes.definition: Walk the owner through each coverage objective on screen and get written acceptance: every zone from the objectives map demonstrated live and in playback; accepted blind spots restated aloud so nobody rediscovers them after a theft; capability honesty about what identification the pixel math actually supports at which spots, with no implied promises beyond it; the retention and access decisions restated in plain language, together with the signage and disclosure duties the owner personally carries, flagged verify-locally; deviations from the design spec listed with reasons; and a signed acceptance that starts the subscription relationship on demonstrated fact. Overselling at walkthrough poisons the recurring relationship the whole business model depends on - the honest demo is also the retention strategy.

excluded: contract and subscription terms, which the offer KB owns
training beyond basic viewing and export

pros.claim: Demonstrated-objective acceptance prevents expectation disputes months later
pros.example: the owner who watched the yard detection demo and signed the accepted-gap list does not claim the system failed when the uncovered side alley is hit

cons.claim: An honest walkthrough can shrink the perceived value the sale implied
cons.example: showing that the parking overview cannot read plates deflates an owner who assumed it would, and the conversation must be had anyway

failure_modes: demonstrating live views only and never playback or export
letting enthusiasm imply identification capability the math does not support
collecting a signature without restating the accepted gaps
acceptance_tests: a signed acceptance exists listing each demonstrated objective, the restated accepted gaps, the capability-honesty notes and any deviations with reasons
revisit_triggers: the owner disputes coverage after an incident
a change order alters zones or objectives

base.update_signal: a post-incident coverage dispute or a change order re-opens the acceptance record

nodes.definition: Deliver the unglamorous documents that make the site operable for years: a per-camera schedule (location name, model, serial, firmware version at commissioning, IP address, vault reference for credentials, mounting photo, field-of-view screenshot by day and by night), the switch port map matching the cable labels, a network diagram with VLANs and firewall intent, the sizing sheet and recorded architecture decision, the retention and access policy as actually configured, the commissioning report with results, and warranty and spares notes. This package is the handoff contract to the operations side - the sibling operations KB starts from it - and the test is simple: a site that cannot be serviced from its documents alone will bleed subscription margin on every future ticket.

included: camera schedule with vault references and FOV screenshots
port map, network diagram, sizing sheet, configured policies
excluded: running the monitoring and retention regime, which operations owns
customer-facing marketing material

pros.claim: A complete as-built package turns future service into lookup work
pros.example: a remote technician resolves a camera-offline ticket from the port map and vault reference without a site visit or a call to whoever installed it

cons.claim: Documentation is the first task cut under end-of-job fatigue
cons.example: the final site of a busy week hands over with photos on a phone and the port map in one technician's head

failure_modes: credentials stored in a text file instead of vault references
FOV screenshots skipped, so aim drift after a storm has no baseline
the port map diverging from re-punched reality and never updated
acceptance_tests: the as-built package contains every listed artifact and a technician unfamiliar with the site can locate any camera, port and credential from it alone
revisit_triggers: any post-handover change to cameras, network or policies
an operations ticket reveals a document/reality mismatch

base.update_signal: a document/reality mismatch found in service or any post-handover change requires the package to be updated

nodes.definition: Consolidate survey, objectives map, lawful screen, camera schedule, placement plan, architecture decision, sizing sheet, retention and access decisions and takeover verdicts into one design spec that three consumers can rely on: the offer side prices from it (its sibling KB owns pricing - this package states counts, labor classes and assumptions, never prices), the install crew builds from it without designer phone calls, and the commissioning checklist is generated from it. Assumptions are recorded explicitly - the measured uplink figure and its date, landlord permissions, accepted gaps, every verify-locally flag - so a later dispute reads decisions, not memories, and a change lands as a numbered revision instead of a verbal drift.

included: single consolidated design package with recorded assumptions
handoffs to offer, install crew and commissioning
excluded: prices and margins, which the offer KB computes from this package
as-built records, which document what was actually installed

pros.claim: One revision-controlled package keeps sale, install and commissioning aligned on the same facts
pros.example: when the owner adds a container yard mid-project, revision two updates counts, sizing and the commissioning checklist together instead of three artifacts drifting apart

cons.claim: The package adds process weight that tiny jobs feel disproportionately
cons.example: a single-camera add-on to an existing site still needs its revision, sizing delta and checklist update to stay trustworthy

failure_modes: verbal changes on site that never land in a revision
assumptions like the uplink measurement date omitted, so nobody knows the sizing is stale
the install crew building from an old revision
acceptance_tests: the design spec contains every upstream artifact, records its assumptions and verify-locally flags, and carries a revision number the install crew and commissioning checklist reference
revisit_triggers: any upstream design node changes its output
a change order arrives from the owner
commissioning or walkthrough feedback contradicts the package

base.update_signal: an upstream design change, a change order, or commissioning feedback forces a new numbered revision

edges.why_related: zone objectives are drawn over the surveyed layout, sight lines and incident history
the uplink is measured on the line and router the site walk discovered
night-scene engineering starts from the survey's day and night lighting notes
reuse verdicts start from the legacy equipment inventory recorded at survey
pixel targets quantify each zone's stated deter/detect/identify purpose
retention classes are assigned per zone objective, evidence zones against ambient views
aims and views may only be fixed inside the lawful screen's allowed envelope
microphone-equipped and covert-styled hardware choices are bounded by the audio-consent and disclosure decisions
retention and viewer-access choices sit under the named data-protection obligation classes
sensor and lens choices execute the zone's on-target density math
height, tilt and distance geometry realizes the density each view needs
the fix-the-scene versus low-light-sensor verdict selects the camera class per zone
the measured uplink budget is the architecture decision's hardest input
retention targets decide how much video must live where and for how long
the sizing math computes the streams and stores the chosen architecture implies
per-camera bitrate class follows from the selected resolution and codec support
the segmentation design passes exactly the flows the chosen architecture needs and nothing else
per-device hardening lands on top of the isolated segment design
each selected model's maximum draw is the power budget's input row
run lengths, power classes and midspan needs decide cable spec and pathing
cable is pulled and certified before final mounting and sealing close everything up
the sizing sheet is a core section of the consolidated design package
the placement plan with heights and aims is written into the package the crew builds from
the retention and access policy is recorded in the package for the operations handoff
keep and retire verdicts with their reasons are recorded in the package
commissioning runs on the finished physical install, not a half-mounted site
hardening spot-checks are a listed part of the commissioning pass
the uplink-pull and catch-up drill validates the sizing sheet's headroom and buffer claims
the owner sees the system only after it has passed its written tests
the commissioning report and recorded firmware versions feed the as-built package
the signed acceptance and agreed deviations are filed into the as-built record
the owner's wanted coverage - break room, neighbor-facing views, covert wishes - collides with the lawful-and-disclosed limits
edges.resolution_rule: the lawful screen always wins: re-aim, relocate or drop the view and record the accepted gap; a covert or privacy-expectation-zone view never ships even at the cost of the sale

edges.why_related: the computed upstream load can exceed the measured uplink budget the site actually has
edges.resolution_rule: the measured budget wins: cut bitrate or frame rate, move zones to event-driven upload, or shift the site to hybrid with an edge buffer; never ship a design whose steady load eats the stated business headroom

edges.why_related: reuse economics pull toward keeping legacy units that cannot meet the hardening baseline
edges.resolution_rule: the baseline wins: units that cannot take unique credentials, current firmware and outbound-only operation are retired regardless of the takeover savings they promised

edges.why_related: at walkthrough the owner asks for identification-grade detail from overview cameras the math never sized for it
edges.resolution_rule: the density math wins: demonstrate the mechanism's limit on screen, then either add a dedicated camera as a numbered change or record the expectation as out of scope; never promise beyond the math verbally

edges.why_related: night gain noise and busy scenes causally inflate bitrate and event counts, moving storage and upload load
night-view or framing failures at commissioning send specific cameras back for re-aiming or relocation
a walkthrough-revealed missed objective re-opens the zone map as a numbered change order
both are the KB's quantitative sizing mechanisms, translating stated objectives into checkable site-specific numbers

conflict_axes.name: coverage_ambition_vs_lawful_disclosure
conflict_axes.description: The owner's wish to see every corner and every person collides with lawful, disclosed surveillance limits on privacy-expectation zones, neighbor overlook and covert devices.
poles: cover everything the owner wants watched
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the lawful screen dominates absolutely; wanted-but-unlawful views become recorded accepted gaps or lawful redesigns, and covert requests are declined

conflict_axes.name: cloud_purity_vs_uplink_reality
conflict_axes.description: The business sells cloud recording, but many sites' measured uplinks cannot carry continuous mainstreams for every camera.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: degrade gracefully to hybrid - edge buffer with event or substream upload - before oversubscribing the line; the measured budget is never exceeded

conflict_axes.name: image_ambition_vs_bitrate_cost
conflict_axes.description: Higher resolution and frame rate improve footage but inflate bitrate, storage and upload load that the uplink and cloud plan must absorb.
poles: minimize bitrate, storage and upload load
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: spend pixels only where the zone purpose demands them and use event-driven recording in ambient zones

conflict_axes.name: few_wide_views_vs_purposeful_density
conflict_axes.description: Fewer wide cameras look economical and tidy but deliver context without identification, while purpose-driven pairs cost more units.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: let the zone purpose decide: identify zones get the pair, ambient zones keep the single wide view

conflict_axes.name: reuse_economics_vs_baseline_integrity
conflict_axes.description: Keeping legacy cameras and cabling cuts the install bill, but unhardenable units and uncertified runs poison the estate the subscription must support.
poles: hold the hardening and certification baseline
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: reuse only what passes the same tests new equipment must pass; the baseline never bends for takeover savings

conflict_axes.name: install_speed_vs_plant_longevity
conflict_axes.description: Finishing the install day fast competes with the sealing, labeling, certification and photographing that prevent years of truck rolls.
poles: build a plant that services cheaply for a decade
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: workmanship steps are checklist items the commissioning gate verifies, not optional polish under schedule pressure

conflict_axes.name: lockdown_vs_serviceability
conflict_axes.description: Tight isolation and hardening protect the estate but make legitimate remote support harder to deliver.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: service travels the same outbound-only platform channel as video, with a documented management path in the as-built package; no inbound holes for convenience

conflict_axes.name: deterrence_visibility_vs_tamper_and_capture
conflict_axes.description: Visible low-mounted cameras deter and capture faces but invite tampering, while high mounts survive attack and record cap tops.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: pair them: protected high context views plus vandal-housed face-height cameras at choke points where identification matters

conflict_axes.name: commissioning_rigor_vs_handover_pressure
conflict_axes.description: The full day-and-night pass with failover drills delays invoicing, and every scheduling pressure pushes toward waving the site through.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: no acceptance walkthrough happens before the commissioning report is complete; a night-check return visit is scheduled at sale time so it is never a surprise cost

edge_cases.description: The uplink tests clean at midday but saturates every evening when the shop runs cloud backups and streams music
edge_cases.trigger: a single quiet-hour measurement is taken as the uplink budget
edge_cases.mitigation: measure at the worst relevant hour, subtract the stated business headroom, and prefer substream-continuous or event upload until the measured budget holds

edge_cases.description: The owner insists on a break-room camera or a hidden device to catch a suspected employee
edge_cases.trigger: a coverage request lands inside a privacy-expectation zone or asks for covert monitoring
edge_cases.mitigation: decline covert and privacy-zone coverage outright, log the declined request, and offer lawful alternatives such as till coverage or a stockroom-door choke point

edge_cases.description: The first after-dark check shows built-in IR bouncing off a near white wall and washing out the entrance view
edge_cases.trigger: a camera commissioned only in daylight meets its real night scene
edge_cases.mitigation: commission every camera after dark as well as by day, and fix failures by re-aiming, off-axis external IR, or a scene lighting change

edge_cases.description: A takeover site runs decade-old coax with unknown-brand analog cameras the owner wants kept for the savings
edge_cases.trigger: reuse pressure lands on legacy plant that was never tested
edge_cases.mitigation: test what integration honestly supports, keep coax only for modest-purpose zones through encoders, rewire identification zones, and put the keep/retire verdicts in writing

edge_cases.description: Cameras reboot randomly on winter nights when IR illuminators and heaters push the switch past its power budget
edge_cases.trigger: PoE was budgeted at idle draw rather than worst-case draw
edge_cases.mitigation: budget from maximum simultaneous draw with headroom and load-test at commissioning with IR forced on

edge_cases.description: The ISP moves the site behind carrier-grade NAT and the remote viewing that relied on port forwarding dies or sits exposed
edge_cases.trigger: an inbound-access design meets CGNAT or a public-address change
edge_cases.mitigation: design outbound-only cloud connectivity from the start: no port forwarding, no UPnP, no vendor peer-to-peer channels beyond the platform's own outbound relay

edge_cases.description: A power blip drops the switch and cameras, and the burglary happens while everything reboots with nothing recorded
edge_cases.trigger: an outage hits a site with no UPS and no edge buffer at that moment
edge_cases.mitigation: put the switch, gateway and any recorder on a UPS sized to the designed buffer window and prove the behavior with the commissioning power-blip drill

edge_cases.description: A glass storefront turns daytime entrance faces into silhouettes against street glare
edge_cases.trigger: a backlit entrance is served by a non-WDR camera or a glare-axis aim
edge_cases.mitigation: specify a WDR-class sensor at the door, aim off the glare axis or add an inward-facing choke-point camera, and verify at the sun's worst angle

edge_cases.description: The customer type - for example a government-adjacent site - forbids certain vendor equipment that the takeover estate contains
edge_cases.trigger: restricted-vendor procurement classes apply to reused or proposed hardware
edge_cases.mitigation: screen models against the customer's applicable procurement classes early - verify current rules locally - and retire non-eligible units before quoting any reuse

edge_cases.description: Motion-event recording tuned too tight misses a slow mover along the fence line; tuned too loose it floods storage and alerts with headlights and cats
edge_cases.trigger: event zones and sensitivity were never walk-tested at their edges
edge_cases.mitigation: walk-test zone edges at commissioning by day and night, tune sensitivity per scene, and re-check the resulting event volume against the sizing sheet

edge_cases.description: The owner expects readable license plates from the wide parking overview camera
edge_cases.trigger: a plate-reading expectation lands on a camera the density math sized for context
edge_cases.mitigation: show the on-target pixel arithmetic, then either add a dedicated tight fast-shutter camera on the gate as a numbered change or record plate capture as out of scope

workflow.action: Walk the site and measure the uplink
workflow.description: Capture layout, surfaces, power, lighting day and night, legacy equipment, constraints, and a worst-relevant-hour upstream measurement
workflow.artifact: survey record with photos, sketch and dated uplink measurement
workflow.gate: layout, power, mounting, incident history, constraint notes and the peak-hour upstream figure are all recorded

workflow.description: Assign each zone a deter/detect/identify purpose and write down accepted gaps
workflow.artifact: zone objective map with accepted-gap list
workflow.gate: every zone carries a purpose and the accepted gaps are documented for signature

workflow.description: Screen all wanted views against privacy-expectation zones, neighbor overlook and the audio-consent decision, stamping the verify-locally flag
workflow.artifact: lawful-placement checklist with jurisdiction flags and the audio decision
workflow.gate: no privacy-expectation zone is covered, the audio decision is recorded, and the verify-locally flag is on the design

workflow.action: Set pixel-density targets and select cameras
workflow.description: Derive per-zone density targets from measured distances against the DORI reference, then match sensor, lens, form factor and illumination to each zone
workflow.artifact: camera schedule written against zone objectives
workflow.gate: each zone's target density has a matching camera and lens choice with its reasoning stated

workflow.action: Fix placement geometry and the lighting plan
workflow.description: Set exact mount points, heights and tilts with choke-point pairs at entrances and per-view night-scene verdicts
workflow.artifact: placement plan with heights, tilts and scene verdicts
workflow.gate: entrances show in-and-out pairing, no view frames the horizon, and every view has a night-scene verdict

workflow.action: Choose the recording architecture and run the sizing math
workflow.description: Decide edge, cloud or hybrid per the measured uplink and retention targets, then size bitrates, storage and upstream load with headroom
workflow.artifact: architecture decision record and sizing sheet
workflow.gate: the summed upstream load fits the measured uplink budget minus headroom and the retention target is met by the storage plan

workflow.action: Design segmentation and the hardening baseline
workflow.description: Put cameras on an isolated segment with outbound-only flows and write the per-device hardening checklist
workflow.gate: cameras sit on an isolated segment with outbound-only cloud flows, and the baseline lists unique credentials, firmware, services, transport and NTP items

workflow.description: Consolidate objectives, lawful screen, camera schedule, placement, architecture, sizing, retention/access and takeover verdicts into one revision-controlled package
workflow.gate: every objective maps to a camera, assumptions and verify-locally flags are recorded, and the package carries a revision number

workflow.action: Install power, cabling and mounts to standard
workflow.description: Build the physical plant: max-draw power budget honored, runs sealed, labeled and certified, mounts anchored, sealed and leveled, photos taken
workflow.artifact: installed plant with certification results and install photos
workflow.gate: the power sheet holds at max draw, every run is labeled and certified, and each mount passes the sealed-and-level photo check

workflow.action: Commission by day and night with the failover drill
workflow.description: Run the written per-camera and site-level pass: framing day and night, event tuning, cloud clip retrieval, timestamps, uplink-pull, power-blip, monitoring registration, hardening spot-checks
workflow.gate: every camera and every site-level drill passes, with failures looped back and re-tested rather than waved through

workflow.action: Walk the owner through and take acceptance
workflow.description: Demonstrate each objective live and in playback, restate accepted gaps, capability limits, retention/access decisions and the owner's disclosure duties
workflow.artifact: signed acceptance with deviations and restated gaps
workflow.gate: each objective is demonstrated and the signed record lists gaps, capability-honesty notes and deviations

workflow.action: Hand the as-built package to operations
workflow.description: Deliver the camera schedule, port map, network diagram, sizing sheet, configured policies, commissioning report and warranty notes to the recurring service
workflow.gate: a technician unfamiliar with the site can locate any camera, port and credential from the package alone

dominance_rules.rule: The lawful-placement boundary dominates every coverage ambition
dominance_rules.rationale: an unlawful or covert view exposes the owner and the installer to liability and destroys the evidence value of the footage
dominance_rules.trigger: a wanted view touches a privacy-expectation zone, a neighbor's private space, or arrives as a covert request
dominance_rules.action: re-aim, relocate or drop the view, record the accepted gap, and decline covert requests outright

dominance_rules.rule: The measured uplink budget dominates cloud-recording ambition
dominance_rules.rationale: an oversubscribed uplink degrades both the video service and the customer's own business traffic
dominance_rules.trigger: the sizing sheet's upstream load approaches or exceeds the measured budget minus headroom
dominance_rules.action: cut bitrates, move zones to event upload, or shift to hybrid with an edge buffer before anything ships

dominance_rules.rule: Pixel-density purpose math dominates promised outcomes
dominance_rules.rationale: footage that cannot serve its stated purpose is a refund conversation and a reputation wound
dominance_rules.trigger: a sale or walkthrough conversation implies identification a zone's math does not support
dominance_rules.action: correct the promise against the math, and add a dedicated camera as a numbered change if the capability is truly wanted

dominance_rules.rule: The hardening baseline dominates reuse economics
dominance_rules.rationale: one unhardenable camera can hand the whole estate and the customer's network to an attacker
dominance_rules.trigger: a legacy unit fails the credential, firmware or provenance tests but the reuse savings look attractive
dominance_rules.action: retire the unit and record the reason; the baseline never bends for takeover savings

dominance_rules.rule: Max-draw power budgeting dominates idle-draw convenience
dominance_rules.rationale: power failures surface at winter nightfall, exactly when cameras exist to work
dominance_rules.trigger: a PoE budget or UPS size is computed from idle draws
dominance_rules.action: recompute from maximum simultaneous draw with headroom and re-select the switch or UPS if needed

dominance_rules.rule: Design-time retention and access decisions dominate sort-it-out-later
dominance_rules.rationale: retention drives sizing and sits under proportionality obligation classes; defaults chosen by accident satisfy neither
dominance_rules.trigger: a design reaches sizing or commissioning without a stated retention and access policy
dominance_rules.action: stop and fix the policy with the owner, then re-run sizing before the design advances

dominance_rules.rule: The commissioning report dominates handover pressure
dominance_rules.rationale: a site waved through untested becomes the operations team's chronic ticket generator and the customer's first churn reason
dominance_rules.trigger: invoice or schedule pressure pushes to skip night checks or the failover drill
dominance_rules.action: hold the acceptance walkthrough until the written pass is complete; schedule the night visit at sale time so it is never a surprise

dominance_rules.rule: Disclosed-surveillance purpose dominates any covert request
dominance_rules.rationale: the business exists to deter, detect and evidence for property owners lawfully; covert monitoring is a different and unlawful trade
dominance_rules.trigger: any request for hidden devices or monitoring beyond the owner's property interest
dominance_rules.action: decline, log the request, and walk away from the work if the customer insists

dominance_rules.rule: The verify-locally flag dominates template reuse across jurisdictions
dominance_rules.rationale: placement, consent and signage obligation classes differ sharply between jurisdictions and change over time
dominance_rules.trigger: a proven design template is about to ship in a new jurisdiction or after a rule change
dominance_rules.action: re-run the lawful-placement screen against current local rules before the template is offered

anti_rework_rules.rule: Measure the uplink at the worst relevant hour before choosing the recording architecture
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-architecting the whole recording plan after cloud uploads backlog in the first week

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run the lawful-placement screen before drawing the placement plan
anti_rework_rules.prevents: redrawing coverage and re-mounting hardware after a forbidden view must be pulled

anti_rework_rules.rule: Set pixel-density targets before selecting cameras
anti_rework_rules.prevents: swapping cameras after the first incident proves the footage useless for its purpose

anti_rework_rules.rule: Assess every scene after dark before finalizing lighting and camera choices
anti_rework_rules.prevents: post-install IR retrofits and camera swaps when the night scene fails

anti_rework_rules.rule: Budget PoE at maximum simultaneous draw before ordering switches
anti_rework_rules.prevents: swapping the switch after winter-night reboots start

anti_rework_rules.rule: Agree retention days and the viewer list before sizing storage and the cloud plan
anti_rework_rules.prevents: resizing plans and renegotiating with the owner after commissioning

anti_rework_rules.rule: Test integration and hardening on actual legacy units before quoting any reuse
anti_rework_rules.prevents: mid-install surprises when kept cameras refuse the platform or the baseline

anti_rework_rules.rule: Label and photograph cable runs during the pull, not afterwards
anti_rework_rules.prevents: wall-opening archaeology on every future fault

anti_rework_rules.rule: Retrieve a cloud clip from every camera before the customer walkthrough
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a failed demonstration and a repeat visit to rebuild trust

iteration_protocol.trigger: a commissioning check fails - night view, framing, event tuning, clip retrieval or the failover drill
iteration_protocol.action: fix at the responsible node (placement, lighting, architecture or hardening) and re-run the failed checks before handover

iteration_protocol.trigger: the measured uplink changes or post-install bitrates and event volumes deviate from the sizing sheet
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the bandwidth and storage math and revisit the architecture choice if the budget no longer holds

iteration_protocol.trigger: the walkthrough reveals a missed objective or an expectation beyond the design
iteration_protocol.action: re-open the zone map and design spec as a numbered change order and re-demonstrate after the change

iteration_protocol.trigger: a jurisdiction changes its placement, audio-consent or signage rules
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the lawful-placement screen on every active design and template in that jurisdiction

iteration_protocol.trigger: a vulnerability advisory or vendor restriction lands on a deployed model class
iteration_protocol.action: update the hardening baseline, patch or retire affected units, and amend the commissioning checklist

iteration_protocol.trigger: the premises change - remodel, new racking, new lighting, new tenancy
iteration_protocol.action: re-survey the affected zones and walk the change through objectives, placement and sizing

iteration_protocol.trigger: operations reports recurring camera-health faults that trace back to install quality
iteration_protocol.action: audit the cabling and mounting standard against the faulting sites and update the install checklist

priority_rationale: The frame nodes - survey, coverage objectives, lawful boundary and uplink measurement - come first because every later choice stands on the site's facts, the owner's stated purposes and the legal envelope; density math, camera, placement, lighting and takeover decisions turn the frame into a buildable design; architecture, sizing, retention and the consolidated spec make it operable and honest against the measured uplink; segmentation, hardening, power, cabling and mounting build it safely and durably; and commissioning, acceptance and as-built handoff come last because they prove and record what was actually delivered to the recurring service.
